newsitem.title: POLAND: ING Barings sees Warsaw bourse weaker.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sees Warsaw bourse weaker.

text.p: ING Barings in London sees the Warsaw bourse weakening in the next few months, possibly pulled down by expected underperformance of banks due to a likely slowdown in their earnings growth, ING said in a March report.
ING Barings said in its Eastern European monthly report it expected the main all-share WIG index, currently at 16,690.4 points to stabilise below 17,000 in the second quarter of 1997.

It said that even though industrial EPS growth of 23.7 percent in nominal terms well exceeded the growth expected for banks, many large cap stocks appeared fully valued and also uncertainty about export performance would weaken sentiment.
ING Barings said it had reduced nominal banking sector earnings per share growth forecast for this year to 14.4 percent from 18.9 percent, which represents a real decline of 1.1 percent.
"For the market as a whole the adjustment to bank earnings forecasts reduces our prospective 1997 EPS growth from 20.6 percent last month to 17.8 percent at present," it said.

It said the lower earnings forecast reflected an expected reduction in interest spread by an average 50bp and said the average real ROE for 1996 was only 1.9 percent and was expected to fall to 0.5 percent in 1997.

ING Barings advised investors to take profits on selected banking stocks, primarily BRE after its 24.4 percent gains and WBK, the most expensive bank on the exchange trading at a 200 percent premium to 1996 book value.

It said Komunalny was the most attractive bank at present with earnings growth six percent above the sector average and valued at 2.2 times 1996 book value with a four percent yield and rated it as accumulate.
